finding.title: Update docs/delete-policy.md — curriculum_tracks moved from deletedAt to state/stateChangedAt in W3.28/W3.29
finding.rule: AG-8 (schema diffs update their paired doc in the same PR) / Tier-4 canonical-doc factual drift

evidence.quote: replaced ad-hoc `isActive`/`deletedAt`/`deactivatedAt` tombstone columns with a single unified `state` enum column

finding.why: curriculum_tracks has no `deletedAt` column at all today — it was replaced by `state`/`stateChangedAt`. A reader implementing new delete-policy-adjacent code from this doc would query/write a column that doesn't exist. The same doc's coverage table also never mentions daily_plans/point_configs/profile_programs/study_day_configs/outbox/curriculum_scopes/prior_completion_imports, all of which track_dao.dart and profile_repository_impl.dart delete explicitly.
finding.recommendation: Update the table row to 'state = deleted + stateChangedAt'; consider adding rows for the other tables track_dao.dart/profile_repository_impl.dart already delete explicitly so the doc is a complete map of delete behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Doc's column-name claim matches an actual column in the current schema (grep-checkable).

finding.title: Delete vestigial .gitkeep from core/database/tables/
finding.why: .gitkeep exists only to keep an otherwise-empty directory tracked; this directory holds 27 real table files, so the placeholder is pure clutter.
acceptance_criteria: File removed; directory remains tracked (trivially true — it has real files).

finding.title: Declare PointsLedger.redemptionId as a real FK to RewardRedemptions instead of a comment-only reference
finding.rule: profileId-in-PK-adjacent referential-integrity discipline / Evans (invariant enforced in one place, not just documented)

evidence.quote: /// Optional FK to [RewardRedemptions.id] for redemption-related entries.

finding.why: The comment asserts a foreign-key relationship the schema never declares. Nothing stops redemptionId from pointing at a nonexistent row, or (with no DB check) at a redemption belonging to a different profile if a future query bug wires the wrong id.
finding.recommendation: Add `.references(RewardRedemptions, #id)` in a schema migration (RewardRedemptions rows are never hard-deleted today, so KeyAction.noAction/restrict is reasonable).
acceptance_criteria: Migration adds the FK; a new test asserts inserting a PointsLedger row with a bogus redemptionId fails.

finding.title: Make ScheduleSpec's delayDays/daysOfWeek/rollingWindowSize getters exhaustive instead of using a `_` catch-all
finding.why: EH-6 requires sealed-type switches to be exhaustive with no `default:`/`_` arm, precisely so the compiler forces every call site to be revisited when a new subtype is added. All three convenience getters on the sealed ScheduleSpec base class use `_ =>` to cover 'the other two variants' instead of naming them. The file's own docstring says a W3.27 migration to a single JSON `schedule` column is coming and will touch this exact codec — when that (or any future) change adds a 4th ScheduleSpec variant, these three getters will compile cleanly and silently return 0/null/null for it instead of forcing a compile error, which is exactly the failure mode sealed classes exist to prevent.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite each getter with an explicit arm per subtype (e.g. `WeeklySchedule() => 0, RollingSchedule() => 0` instead of `_ => 0`) so adding a new variant breaks the build until these getters are updated.
acceptance_criteria: delayDays/daysOfWeek/rollingWindowSize each list DelaySchedule/WeeklySchedule/RollingSchedule explicitly with no `_`/`default` arm.

Once dart run custom_lint is fixed (already tracked separately), no_hardcoded_domain_term-style exhaustiveness stays enforced; until then, `dart analyze` continues to flag any genuinely non-exhaustive switch if a variant is later added without updating these getters.

finding.title: Fix SefariaRef.titlePart/addressPart to match the documented chapter:verse split (or fix the docs)
finding.rule: Evans (ubiquitous-language contract) / TQ-7-TQ-8 spirit (test encodes the bug instead of catching it)
finding.why: The class docstring's own worked example says titlePart of "Mishnah Berakhot 1:1" is "Mishnah Berakhot" (address "1:1"). The `_splitTail` regex only strips a single trailing digit run (optionally +1 letter), so it can never cross the ':' in a chapter:verse address — for that exact documented example it actually produces titlePart == "Mishnah Berakhot 1:" and addressPart == "1". The test file's own inline comment ('let's assert what we actually produce... The SefariaRef titlePart splits on the LAST pure-numeric token') shows the author noticed the mismatch and wrote the test to lock in the wrong output rather than fix the regex or the docs. Mishnah/Tanach chapter:verse is the single most common ref shape in this Torah-study app, so any future caller of titlePart/addressPart (currently unused in production) inherits silently wrong output for the primary case, with a green regression test giving false confidence.
finding.recommendation: Either extend `_splitTail` to also recognize a `\d+:\d+` chapter:verse tail as one address token, or correct the docstring to describe the actual single-digit-run behavior — then update the test to assert the corrected contract, not the current output.
acceptance_criteria: SefariaRef.parse('Mishnah Berakhot 1:1').titlePart equals whatever the corrected docstring promises (either 'Mishnah Berakhot' with the regex fixed, or the docstring rewritten to match current behavior).
sefaria_ref_test.dart's titlePart test for chapter:verse refs no longer contains a comment acknowledging the assertion doesn't match the documented contract.
